name: Kasem
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Niggli, Urs & Idda Niggli. 2008. Grammaire elementaire du kasim. SIL Burkina Faso (phonology section; Kasem is a 3-tone language per Wikipedia summary read); grammar PDF not reachable

sources.citation: Pike, Kenneth L. 1966. Tagmemic and matrix linguistics applied to selected African languages. Final report. (ERIC ED010547; Kasem appendices by John & Kathleen Callow).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kasem material is clause/serial-construction and nominal/verbal matrices only; the volume's only word-stress rule (stress on highest-toned syllable) is in the Agbo (Legbo) appendix, not Kasem. Cites Callow 1965 'Collected field reports on the phonology of Kasem' as the Kasem phonology source.

sources.citation: Callow, John C. 1965. Kasem nominals: a study in analyses. Journal of West African Languages 2(1): 29-36.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: scanned. Treats the grammatical word as a phonological unit defined by vowel harmony and the distribution of tone and nasality (fn. 12: 'vowel harmony, nasalisation, and pitch'); stress is never mentioned.

sources.citation: SIL Burkina Faso. Bibliographie kassena (13 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography; used to identify Awedoba 2002, Bonvini 1974, Callow 1965, Cremer 1924 as the phonology-bearing works.

sources.citation: Niggli, Urs & Idda Niggli. 2008. Grammaire élémentaire du kasɩm. 2e éd. Ouagadougou: Société Internationale de Linguistique (SIL). 117 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Ch. 1 'Rappel phonologique' (pp. 5-11) covers consonants, vowels, vowel harmony, long vowels, vowel sequences and 1.7 'Les tons' (three level tones: bas, moyen, haut; lexical and grammatical function). No mention of stress/accent d'intensité anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent; tone page read as image).

sources.citation: StressTyp2 v1 archive (2015 SQL dump, local copy) and WALS CLDF
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kasem (xsm) appears only in the StressTyp2 ISO code table -- no stress entry; WALS has no phonology features (13A-17A) coded for ksm.

sources.citation: SIL Burkina Faso [U. & I. Niggli]. 2005. Guide d'orthographe kasɩm. 3e éd. Ouagadougou: SIL. 60 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Alphabet, consonants, vowels, harmony, vowel sequences, spelling rules; sec. 9 'Mots avec accent' is about the acute accent used to write high tone on four grammatical words. Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Niggli, Urs & Idda Niggli. [1994/2000s]. Premiers pas en kasɩm (language primer). Ouagadougou: SIL. 56 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pronunciation guide and tone notes (low, rising, mid, high); one remark on question intonation (lengthened final syllable with falling intonation). Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Awedoba, A. K. 1990. Kasem tones and orthography. Journal of West African Languages 20(2): 31-46.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Scanned; scanned with tesseract. Describes the tone system (levels, grammatical tone, no downdrift), segment inventory (19 C, 10 V), CV syllable preference, short words; 'accent' only in the sense of French orthographic diacritics. No statement about stress.

sources.citation: Kẽdrebéogo, Gérard & Zakaria Yago. 1986. Langues du Burkina Faso: les langues gurunsi. Ouagadougou: CNRST.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative wordlists (kasim, nuni, lyele, pana); no phonology prose, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bonvini, Emilio. 1983-1995. 'Linguistique africaine' (rapports de conférences). Annuaires de l'EPHE IVe section (1983, 1989, 1990, 1992, 1995).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Seminar reports on Kasim nominal/verbal grammar, negation, serial verbs; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bonvini, Emilio. 1972. La phonologie du kàsim [position de thèse]. Annuaire de l'École pratique des hautes études, IVe section, 1971-1972: 745-747.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Three-page summary of the thesis later published as Bonvini 1974: syllable defined by tonality (oppositional) and modulation and length (contrastive); phonological word defined via vowel harmony. No mention of accent/stress.

sources.citation: mabia-vp.com, 'Kasem' page (VP-periphery in Mabia languages project).
sources.note: States only 'Kasem has a three level tone system with a low tone, a high tone and a mid level tone' (citing Niggli & Niggli 2008); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hewer, Philip L. 1983. A basic grammar of Kasem. Tamale: Ghana Institute of Linguistics, Literacy and Bible Translation (GILLBT).

sources.note: GILLBT grammar of Ghanaian Kasem; likely has a short phonology/orthography chapter that may mention stress vs tone.

sources.citation: Callow, John C. 1965. Collected field reports on the phonology of Kasem (Collected Language Notes 1). Legon: Institute of African Studies, University of Ghana / SIL. 95 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: Pike-school SIL phonology write-up (phoneme, syllable, phonological word, stress group hierarchy); this series routinely contains an explicit 'stress' paragraph. Cited by Pike 1966 as the Kasem phonology source. May exist as a scan in the SIL archive (sil.org, could not be reached by automated download).

sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: The only book-length modern phonetics/phonology of Kasem; if any source states whether Kasem has word stress (and where it falls) alongside the three tones, it is this one. Would supersede everything found.

sources.note: Full Martinet-school phonology of Burkina Kasim with chapters on the syllable (tonality, modulation, length) and the 'mot phonologique'; any statement on accent (or its explicit absence) would be there.

sources.citation: Cremer, Jean (éd. Maurice Delafosse). 1924. Grammaire de la langue kasséna ou kassené, parlée au pays des Gourounsi. Paris: Geuthner. 64 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Oldest grammar; colonial-era French grammars often carry an 'accent tonique' remark. US public domain (1924) so a HathiTrust/Google full view may exist; HathiTrust and Google Books were bot-could not be reached by automated download and it is not on Gallica or archive.org.
